claims.statement: `nodemw` is the only MediaWiki client dependency, declared once as `"nodemw": "^0.26.0"` and locked at 0.26.0; because a caret range on a 0.x version admits only same-minor updates, 0.26.x patches install without a code change while any 0.27 upgrade requires editing package.json.
The integration's Node floor is consistent on both sides: this package declares `node >= 18.0.0`, esbuild targets node18, and nodemw declares `>=18.0`.

`createBotFromConfig` is the only place a nodemw `Bot` is constructed, mapping `ServerConfig` onto the client's options; it forwards `dryRun` behind a `@ts-expect-error` because nodemw honours the option at runtime but omits it from its published `BotOptions` type, so a future release that adds the field turns the suppression into a compile error.

`nodemw` is value-imported exactly once (`import Bot from 'nodemw'` in `src/common/nodemwBot.ts`); `src/common/utils.ts` and `src/common/compareOutput.ts` only do `import type Bot`, and no tool module imports the library at all — handlers reach the client through `getBot()` plus the two bridges (`promisifyBotMethod` from nodemwBot, `callApi` from utils), so replacing the client layer means touching the two common modules.

`promisifyBotMethod` dispatches by string method name — `(bot as any)[method](...args, callback)` — which is what lets call sites invoke methods missing from nodemw's hand-written declarations (such as `delete`) without a cast, at the price of an unchecked `<T>` assertion and runtime-only failure for a renamed method.

The bridge supports only single-value callbacks, resolving the first argument after `err`; nodemw methods that report extra values therefore need hand-written Promises, which is why `get-article`'s `redirectInfo` branch resolves a `(content, redirectInfo)` tuple instead of using the bridge.

Consumption of the same client method varies by parameter, not by tool: `get-article` calls `getArticle` through a hand-rolled Promise resolving a `[content, redirectInfo]` tuple when `redirectInfo` is requested and through `promisifyBotMethod` otherwise, while `edit`, `write`, `revert`, the read guard's `getArticleInfo`/`getArticle` calls and `get-article-with-lineno` use only the bridge, so redirect information is structurally unavailable to them.

`get-log`, `get-recent-changes`, and `get-images` hand-roll promises that resolve only the first non-error callback argument and discard the client's continuation cursor; pagination is instead delegated to a caller-supplied start value plus client-side `limit` slicing with `total`/`displayed` reporting, and all three modules still import `promisifyBotMethod` without calling it.

Four admin tools (`block`, `unblock`, `protect`, `undelete`) call nodemw's `getToken` inside hand-rolled Promises rather than through the bridge even though its `(err, token)` callback would fit, because the token type is computed per call from the cached MediaWiki version.

The tool-facing call surface is not a one-to-one mapping onto nodemw methods: title-addressed single-value reads and every write go through the client's own wrappers (`getSiteInfo`, `getSiteStats`, `getArticleInfo`, `getArticle`, `doEdit`, `delete`, `move`, `purge`, `upload`, `sendEmail`, `createAccount`, `addFlowTopic`), while id-addressed reads, wrappers whose parameters are wrong, wrappers that hardcode removed parameters, and reads needing self-managed pagination go through the raw transport; `move` and `delete` still return the client's action sub-objects, whose field names those tools' result shapes mirror.

Every gap in the client's wrappers is closed through one shared helper, `callApi` in `src/common/utils.ts`, which wraps `(bot as any).api.call(params, cb, 'GET' | 'POST')` in a hand-rolled Promise and resolves the fourth callback argument (the full raw envelope); the cast therefore exists at exactly two sites — `callApi` and `fetchWhoami` — because nodemw declares no `api` member in its typings.

esbuild marks `nodemw`, `@modelcontextprotocol/*`, and `zod` external, so `dist/index.js` still contains `import Bot from "nodemw"` and functions as a thin launcher requiring those packages installed beside it; the shipped artifact's runtime dependency set is therefore decided entirely by `dependencies` plus the lockfile, making a client version bump or a change in how the adapter uses the client a release-level change that the bundle cannot compensate for.

Client and SDK versions are resolved at runtime: `src/server.ts` builds the default User-Agent via `createRequire(import.meta.url)` lookups of `nodemw/package.json` and the MCP SDK's package.json (esbuild drops `with { type: 'json' }` on external modules), so the advertised nodemw version follows the installed dependency, while this package's own version is inlined into the bundle at build time — the committed `dist/index.js` still carrying 0.2.3 against a 0.3.1 `package.json` shows the artifact is only refreshed by an explicit rebuild.

There are no tests that execute real nodemw: vitest suites exist under `src/common/__tests__` and `src/tools/__tests__`, but the tool smoke tests replace the whole `src/common/nodemwBot.js` module with `fakeNodemwBot.ts`, so the client library and the bundled patch are only ever exercised against a live wiki, while `test-server.js` merely asserts `dist/index.js` exists and starts without crashing.

`DEFAULT_USER_AGENT` is assembled in `src/server.ts` from the installed nodemw version, the Node version plus platform/arch, and this package's name and version with the MCP SDK version, deliberately reproducing nodemw's own default User-Agent prefix so code that identifies the library still matches; `createBotFromConfig` then forwards `DEFAULT_USER_AGENT`, `userAgent`, or `DEFAULT_USER_AGENT + ' ' + userAgent`, so a custom UA without `userAgentAppend` fully replaces the default identity and `userAgentAppend` alone has no effect.

The API URL is produced by string concatenation of the options this adapter forwards — `${protocol}://${server}[:port]${path}/api.php` — so `path` must be a bare script-path prefix with no `api.php` and no trailing slash; the server repeats that formula only to build the endpoint shown in its instructions and startup banner, and that copy omits `port`, so a wiki on a non-standard port is advertised at a different URL than the client requests.

`autoDetectPath` probes exactly two prefixes, `/w` and the empty string (i.e. `/w/api.php` and `/api.php`), because the client accepts a single prefix; each candidate builds a throwaway, never-logged-in `Bot` and sends one `getSiteInfo(['general'])` call, the first responder wins, and total failure throws an error that names both URLs and tells the user to pass `--path` explicitly (with `--path /w` or `--path ""` as examples), even though an empty `--path` cannot disable detection because `pathExplicit` is computed by truthiness.

The dry-run guard is not implemented in this repository: `dryRun` is only forwarded to the client under a `@ts-expect-error` and nothing in `src/` reads it back, so write tools inherit protection only by going through the client's guarded wrappers (`doEdit`, `delete`, `move`, `purge`, `upload`, ...) and the admin tools that issue raw `callApi` requests write for real under `--dry-run`.

Handlers reach the client in exactly three wrapper shapes: `promisifyBotMethod`, which dispatches a string method name and resolves only the first callback value; `callApi`, which dispatches the raw transport and resolves the full envelope; and a commented hand-rolled `new Promise` used by the four version-aware `getToken` calls, by `getLog`/`getRecentChanges`/`getImages`, and by `get-article`'s `redirectInfo` branch — so `as any` casts are confined to `callApi`, `fetchWhoami`, and those `getToken` sites.

The bundled patch is applied only by the install lifecycle: `postinstall` runs `patch-package` and `patches/nodemw+0.26.0.patch` is written against the exact upstream version, so under the `^0.26.0` caret any non-0.26.0 install (including a 0.26.x patch release) makes the install fail loudly instead of silently running an unhardened client.

The patch is not part of the repository state — it only ever lands in `node_modules` — so whether an installation is hardened must be checked by grepping the patch markers: this snapshot's `node_modules/nodemw/lib/api.js` is still the unpatched original (it still contains `this.info(process.argv.join(" "))` and has no `timeout: 30000`).

The hardening does not reach npm consumers: `files` ships only `dist` and `patch-package` is declared only in `devDependencies`, so an `npm i @xiedada/nodemw-mcp-server` installation gets neither `patches/` nor the `patch-package` executable, while the published `postinstall` entry can still fail the install in an environment that lacks that binary.

Keeping nodemw external is what makes the patch effective at runtime: because esbuild leaves `nodemw` out of the bundle, the process loads the patched files inside `node_modules`, whereas inlining the library would move patch application from install time to build time and freeze a patched snapshot into the artifact.

Defect class 1 (malformed API responses, CWE-754/248): the patch guards `data.error` and routes falsy bodies to `callback(new Error("MediaWiki API returned an empty response"))`, and guards the response dereferences in `getFirstItem`, `getToken`, `doEdit`, `addFlowTopic`, `delete`, `purge`, `sendEmail`, `move`, `upload`, `createAccount`, `logIn`, and `getMediaWikiVersion` — without it a 200 JSON body of an unexpected shape throws inside `@cypress/request`'s `complete` listener and becomes an uncaughtException for the host.

Defect class 2 (missing request timeouts, CWE-400): the patch adds `timeout: 30000` to both `doRequest` and `fetchUrl`; without it a stalled api.php holds its slot in the shared `async.queue` (default concurrency 3) forever, so three stalled requests freeze all library traffic.

Defect class 3 (session cookie-jar leakage, CWE-200/384): the patch reuses the bot's shared `RequestJar` only when the fetch target matches the wiki's own origin (protocol, hostname, and port) and gives every other target a throwaway jar, because cookie scoping is hostname-based, port-agnostic, and lets `Domain=` cookies match sibling subdomains.

Defect class 4 (argv logging, CWE-532): the patch deletes the `this.info(process.argv.join(" "))` line from the `Api` constructor while keeping the User-Agent and referer log lines, so CLI credentials passed as `-p <password>` or `--token` no longer reach stdout or the conditional log-file transport.

The application-level answer to defect class 1 is a `process.on('uncaughtException')` suppressor registered at startup: nodemw's response callbacks run on `@cypress/request`'s `complete` listener, outside every promise chain and tool `try/catch`, so the suppressor keeps the one-process-one-session MCP channel alive at the cost of leaving the affected tool call hanging until the client times out.

`upload-by-url` never uses nodemw's URL fetching: it downloads through `fetchSourceSafely`, which re-validates the address on every redirect hop, refuses non-http(s) schemes plus `localhost`/`unix`/private-reserved targets, enforces a 50 MB byte cap and a 30 s deadline, and carries no cookie jar — only then does it hand the bytes to `promisifyBotMethod(bot, 'upload', ...)`.

nodemw turns any response carrying a MediaWiki `error` key into `new Error('Error returned by API: ' + data.error.info)`, discarding `error.code`, and the patch leaves that behaviour intact; consequentially the app can only re-route failures by matching message text (`utils.ts`'s login-expiry and edit-conflict patterns, the latter tested against English and Chinese messages) and every `if (raw.error)` branch is defensive code that real nodemw never reaches.

`parse` and `expand-templates` bypass the wrappers because `bot.parse()` / `expandTemplates()` hardcode `generatexml=1` (removed in MW 1.36, and on older versions returning the parse tree instead of expanded wikitext) and because `parse`'s image list arrives as a third callback argument that the single-value bridge drops; both now build their own `action=parse` / `action=expandtemplates` requests through `callApi`.

`get-users` and `protect` bypass their wrappers for parameter defects rather than missing coverage: nodemw's `getUsers` always sends `auwitheditsonly` (0 when no filter is wanted, which MediaWiki still treats as an active filter) so the tool builds `list=allusers` itself, and the `protect` wrapper hardcodes the token type to `csrf`, which necessarily fails on pre-1.24 wikis, so the tool computes `csrf` versus the action-specific token from the cached version and sends the whole `action=protect` request itself.

Most raw-transport reads exist because nodemw's wrappers can only address pages by title or revision by page: `get-article`'s `id`/`revision` branches, `get-article-by-revision` (`revids`), `get-article-with-lineno`'s id branch and its extra request for `revid`/timestamp, the `id` branches of `get-article-info`/`-categories`/`-properties`, and `whois`/`whoare`'s numeric-id branches all issue `pageids`/`revids`/`ususerids` queries through `callApi`.

Self-managed pagination is the other major source of raw calls: `search` needs `srnamespace`, `get-pages-by-prefix` needs `apnamespace` (and the wrapper truncates at the first page), and `get-pages-transcluding` replaces a `getAll` iterator that fails to terminate on older MediaWiki with `list=embeddedin` — all three drive their own `continue` loops over `callApi`.

The offline test double encodes this repository's assumptions about nodemw rather than exercising the library: `fakeNodemwBot.ts` is a `Proxy` whose `api.call` answers with a four-argument `(err, info, next, data)` callback carrying the full envelope and whose other methods answer via a `METHOD_RETURNS` table with a hybrid array-plus-object result delivered on `process.nextTick`.
